## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

# Lab 1: Data Visualization

This lab explores basic plots in R using the `midwest` dataset from the `ggplot2` package.

library(tidyverse) data(midwest)

#Q1: Histogram of population density

hist(midwest\$popdensity, main = "Histogram of Population Density", xlab = "Population Density", col = "skyblue", breaks = 30)

#Q2: Boxplot of area by state

ggplot(midwest, aes(x = state, y = area)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen") + labs(title = "Boxplot of Area by State", x = "State", y = "Area")

#Q3: Scatter plot of total population vs population density

ggplot(midwest, aes(x = poptotal, y = popdensity)) + geom_point(color = "purple") + labs(title = "Total Population vs Population Density", x = "Total Population", y = "Population Density")

#Q4: Scatter plot colored by state

ggplot(midwest, aes(x = poptotal, y = popdensity, color = state)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "Population vs Population Density by State", x = "Total Population", y = "Population Density")

#Q5: Faceted scatter plot by state

ggplot(midwest, aes(x = poptotal, y = popdensity)) + geom_point(color = "orange") + facet_wrap(\~state) + labs(title = "Population vs Density Faceted by State", x = "Total Population", y = "Population Density")
